# NOTE: NISHIJIMA Models
# The final matrix submitted to the XGBoost model may contain NaNs for missing features from the feature set or for any feature that has 0 SD. 
# XGBoost will treat these as truly missing.For example, a taxon that was entirely absent or got replaced with NaN during scaling becomes XGBoost’s “missing” placeholder. What that means is..
# The model has learned to route all missing values to a certain leaf node for any taxa. aka it built decision trees that split on thresholds of individual taxa abundances.
# but it also learned, at each split, what to do if the taxon-column value is missing. That is recorded as the missing= branch in the dump from caret::xgb.dump().
# An example feature might be g_Bacteroides. “missing=3” from caret::xgb.dump() means: if a sample’s g_Bacteroides is NaN→NA, send it to node 3 (the same as “yes”).
# this can be further described as:
# For each internal node, XGBoost checks your sample’s value for the split taxon.
# If the value is finite, it compares to the threshold and goes left or right.
# If the value is NA, it follows the missing= direction.
# Eventually you land in a leaf node, which holds a learned constant.
# XGBoost sums the leaf values from every tree to produce the final prediction for that sample. Even if many taxa are NaN, each tree has a default path for every missing taxon, so you never get an NA prediction—just the sum of all those default‐routed leaf values.

# Summary:
# When you feed XGBoost a microbiome sample that has “holes” (NaNs) in some taxa columns, XGBoost treats each NaN as a bona fide “missing” value and routes it down a pre-learned default branch at every split.
# Each decision tree has recorded, for every taxon split, “if taxon X is missing, go left (or right).” 
# The final prediction is just the sum of all the leaf values reached—so you’ll always get a number, never an error or an NA.

### When a taxon value becomes **`NaN`** in the prediction matrix

| Situation in the abundance table                                     | How XGBoost interprets it                           | Practical consequence                                                                                     |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| *`NaN` produced by your scaling step*  <br>(all log-values identical → 0 s.d.) | “Feature value is **missing**.” The tree follows the hard-coded **`missing=`** branch. | That split no longer depends on the taxon’s true level. If many taxa go `NaN`, the model leans on a reduced, distorted feature set. |
| Taxon truly absent (all zeros) but later coerced to `NaN`             | Also treated as “missing”, **not** “zero”.           | The model can’t distinguish *structural absence* from *unknown*, so biological signal is lost.             |
| Taxon present in training but wholly missing in the new cohort (column of zeros → scaled `NaN`) | Every sample takes the same `missing` branch ⇒ the split collapses to a constant. | Systematic bias: predictions shift because an informative split is now ignored.                            |
| Taxon had 0 s.d. **during training** but still appears in a split     | All training rows already used the `missing` branch! | The split is an artefact; it just adds noise.                                                              |

---

### Why this is **problematic**

1. **Loss of biological meaning** – A genuine zero abundance is informative; a `NaN` is ambiguous.  
2. **Cohort-specific bias** – If an entire study shares the same `NaN` pattern, predictions shift for non-biological reasons.  
3. **Hidden feature drop-out** – Taxa important in training may be silently ignored at inference.  
4. **Illusory confidence** – XGBoost always returns a number, so large missing-value routing often goes unnoticed.

---

### Summary

> In Nishijima2025s caret/XGBoost pipeline each genus-level abundance is a feature.  
> Any `NaN` that leaks in after log-scaling or centring is interpreted by XGBoost as a genuinely *missing* value.  
> At every split the model contains an explicit `missing` branch, so the code never fails; it simply routes the sample down a default path.  
> The danger is that biologically meaningful **zero** abundances or scaler artefacts become indistinguishable ‘unknowns’, causing the model to ignore—or mis-weight—key taxa.  
> If whole cohorts share the same `NaN` pattern, we introduce a cohort-specific prediction bias.

```{r Embedding Space}

# ---- UMAP for covariate shift analysis----
library(uwot)    
library(FNN)   
library(ggnewscale)
library(ggsci)

debug_repo <- lapply(predictionandtruthresults, function(study) {
  study[c("counts", "tax", "scale")] <- NULL
  study$predictions <- clean_nested_dataframes(
    study$predictions,
    exact_names = loadcolumnstoremove,
    substr_patterns = substr_patterns
  )
  study
})
is_empty_counts <- function(x) {
  if (is.null(x)) return(TRUE)
  if (is.atomic(x)) return(all(is.na(x)))
  if (is.data.frame(x)) return(nrow(x) == 0 || all(sapply(x, function(col) all(is.na(col)))))
  if (is.list(x)) return(length(x) == 0 || all(sapply(x, is_empty_counts)))
  FALSE
}
prune_empty_lists <- function(x) {
  if (is.data.frame(x) || !is.list(x)) return(x)
  x <- lapply(x, prune_empty_lists)
  x[!sapply(x, function(el) {
    is.null(el) ||
    (is.atomic(el) && all(is.na(el))) ||
    (is.list(el) && (length(el) == 0 || all(sapply(el, function(y) is.null(y) ||
        (is.atomic(y) && all(is.na(y))) ||
        (is.list(y) && length(y) == 0)))))
  })]
}
debug_repo <- lapply(debug_repo, function(study) {
  if (!is.null(study$proportions) && is.list(study$proportions)) {
    study$proportions <- prune_empty_lists(study$proportions)
  }
  if (is_empty_counts(study$proportions)) return(NULL)
  study
})
debug_repo$Vandeputte2017 <- NULL
debug_repo$Pereira2023$proportions$reprocessed$rdp16 <- NULL
debug_repo$Pereira2023$predictions$reprocessed$rdp16 <- NULL
debug_repo$Krawczyk2022$proportions$original$rdp16 <- NULL
debug_repo$Krawczyk2022$predictions$original$rdp16 <- NULL
debug_repo$Marotz2021$metadata <- debug_repo$Marotz2021$metadata$reprocessed %>% 
  filter(BioProject == "PRJEB34272")
debug_repo$Contijoch2019$metadata <- debug_repo$Contijoch2019$metadata$shotgun
debug_repo$`Contijoch2019 16S`$metadata <- debug_repo$`Contijoch2019 16S`$metadata$amplicon
debug_repo <- Filter(Negate(is.null), debug_repo)
debug_repo <- lapply(debug_repo, function(study) {
  if (!is.null(study$proportions)) study$proportions <- prune_empty_lists(study$proportions)
  if (!is.null(study$predictions)) study$predictions <- prune_empty_lists(study$predictions)
  study
})
debug_repo <- Filter(function(study) {
  !is_empty_counts(study$proportions) && !is_empty_counts(study$predictions)
}, debug_repo)
extract_leaf_df <- function(x) {
  if (is.data.frame(x)) return(x)
  if (is.list(x) && all(sapply(x, is.atomic))) return(as.data.frame(x))
  if (is.list(x)) {
    for (el in x) {
      df <- extract_leaf_df(el)
      if (!is.null(df)) return(df)
    }
  }
  NULL
}
repo <- lapply(debug_repo, function(study) {
  study$proportions <- extract_leaf_df(study$proportions)
  study$predictions <- extract_leaf_df(study$predictions)
  study
})
amplicon <- keep(repo, ~ tolower(.x$studydemographics$sequencingtype) == "16s rrna")

model       = readRDS("R/microbial_load_predictor/inst/extdata/16S_rRNA/model.16S_rRNA.rds")
xgb_mod      <- model$finalModel
feature_cols <- xgb_mod$feature_names
modelfeatures <- setdiff(feature_cols, ".outcome")

all_studies_wide <- imap_dfr(amplicon, function(study_obj, study_name) {
  prop_mat <- t(study_obj$proportions)
  pred_df <- study_obj$predictions %>%
    { if ("sample ID" %in% colnames(.)) . else rownames_to_column(., var = "sample ID") }
  sample_ids <- unique(pred_df$`sample ID`)
  prop_long <- as.data.frame(prop_mat) %>%
    rownames_to_column("feature") %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols        = -feature,
      names_to    = "sample ID",
      values_to   = "value"
    ) %>%
    filter(feature %in% modelfeatures)

  prop_wide <- prop_long %>%
    pivot_wider(
      names_from  = feature,
      values_from = value,
      values_fill = 0
    )
  prop_wide <- tibble(`sample ID` = sample_ids) %>%
    left_join(prop_wide, by = "sample ID") %>%
    mutate(across(-`sample ID`, ~ replace_na(.x, 0)))
  missing_feats <- setdiff(modelfeatures, colnames(prop_wide))
  for (f in missing_feats) prop_wide[[f]] <- 0
  prop_wide <- prop_wide %>% select(`sample ID`, all_of(modelfeatures))
  input    <- prop_wide %>% select(-`sample ID`)
  input.min <- min(input[input != 0]) / 2
  scaled_mat <- input %>%
    { scale(log10(. + input.min)) } %>%
    as.data.frame()
  scaled_mat = input
  prop_wide <- bind_cols(tibble(`sample ID` = prop_wide$`sample ID`), scaled_mat)
  joined <- left_join(prop_wide, pred_df, by = "sample ID") %>%
    mutate(study = study_name)
  truth_cols <- grep("^log10_truth_", names(joined), value = TRUE)
  loadtypes  <- study_obj$studydemographics$loadtype %||% NA_character_

  map_dfr(truth_cols, function(truth_col) {
    lt_val <- infer_loadtype(truth_col, loadtypes)

    joined %>%
      mutate(
        Truth     = .data[[truth_col]],
        Predicted = log10_mlp
      ) %>%
      select(`sample ID`, study, all_of(modelfeatures), Predicted, Truth) %>%
      filter(is.finite(Truth)) %>%
      mutate(
        Residual   = mean_center(Predicted) - mean_center(Truth),
        Truth_Col  = truth_col,
        loadtype   = lt_val
      ) %>%
      group_by(study) %>%
      ungroup()
  })
}) %>%
  mutate(rowname = paste0(study, "_", `sample ID`, "_", loadtype)) 

all_studies_wide <- all_studies_wide %>%
  left_join(status_df, by = c("study", "loadtype")) 

all_studies_wide <- all_studies_wide %>%
  mutate(across(
    all_of(modelfeatures),
    ~ replace(.x, is.nan(.x), 0)
  )) %>%
  filter(if_any(all_of(modelfeatures), ~ .x != 0)) %>%
  group_by(study) %>%
  distinct(across(all_of(modelfeatures)), .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!(Truth_Col %in% c("log10_truth_DNS_bacterial_load", "log10_truth_TI_bacterial_load", "log10_truth_qpcr_median_16s_copies_per_2ul_dna", 
                            "log10_truth_all_flow_cells_5min_avg", "log10_truth_qpcr_copies_ul")))
                                    

df_fc <- all_studies_wide %>% 
  filter(!grepl("its", Truth_Col, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>%
  group_by(study, Truth_Col) %>%
  mutate(
    pearson = cor(
      mean_center(Predicted),
      mean_center(Truth),
      use = "complete.obs"
    ),
    r2 = {
      centred_pred <- mean_center(Predicted)
      centred_truth <- mean_center(Truth)
      sse <- sum((centred_pred - centred_truth)^2)
      sst <- sum(centred_truth^2)
      round(1 - sse / sst, 2)
    }
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

feature_mat <- df_fc %>%
  select(all_of(modelfeatures)) %>%
  as.matrix()

library(rnndescent)

  tsne_df <- as_tibble(tsne_res$Y) %>%
    setNames(c("Dim1","Dim2")) %>%
    bind_cols(df_fc)

  tsne_df <- tsne_df %>%

  p_resid <- ggplot()+

  print(p_resid)
```
